findings.title: Inadequate Synchronization of Shared Data
findings.trigger: Multiple threads pushing and popping from the queue concurrently
findings.assumptions: The `prot_queue` implementation does not provide any synchronization mechanism to handle concurrent access. If multiple threads are accessing the queue simultaneously, it may lead to data corruption or race conditions.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.assumptions: The `prot_queue` implementation does not handle overflow conditions properly. If the loop counter exceeds the buffer size, it may lead to buffer overflows or other undefined behavior.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
findings.trigger: Untrusted data being used in a SQL query
findings.assumptions: The `prot_queue_pop` function may be used to retrieve data that is then used in an SQL query. If the data is not properly sanitized, it may lead to SQL injection attacks.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: Untrusted data being used in an OS command
findings.assumptions: The `prot_queue_pop` function may be used to retrieve data that is then used in an OS command. If the data is not properly sanitized, it may lead to OS command injection attacks.
